fixes.explanation: That's it! God says, "…the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel." (Ezekiel 48:31) Twelve gates, three on each side, and every one carries a tribe's name. The north side has "the gate of Reuben, the gate of Judah, and the gate of Levi." That's a whole city with the family name on the door.

I see why Judah jumped out, it's a big name. But Judah gets one portion, the last strip before the set-apart land (Ezekiel 48:7). The name with two portions is Joseph (Ezekiel 47:13), and his sons Manasseh and Ephraim (Genesis 41:51-52) show up in the tribe list later (Ezekiel 48:4-5).

The sanctuary, yes! God says of the set-apart portion, "In the center will be the sanctuary." (Ezekiel 48:8) Verse 10 says it again: "In the center will be the sanctuary of the LORD." So it sits right in the middle of the portion set apart.
A fortress isn't what the text puts at the center, friend. It says, "In the center will be the sanctuary." (Ezekiel 48:8) And verse 10 calls it "…the sanctuary of the LORD."

That's right! God says it is for "…the descendants of Zadok, who kept My charge…" (Ezekiel 48:11) Those are the consecrated priests. God adds that they "did not go astray as the Levites did when the Israelites went astray."

Sell, that's the first blank! God says, "They must not sell or exchange any of it, and they must not transfer this best part of the land…" (Ezekiel 48:14) That means no selling, no swapping and no handing it over.

False is right! The text says, "The workers of the city who cultivate it will come from all the tribes of Israel." (Ezekiel 48:19) Not one tribe, but all of them. That's a lot of different hands on the city's land.

False is right! The east side has "the gate of Joseph, the gate of Benjamin, and the gate of Dan." (Ezekiel 48:32) Manasseh and Ephraim, Joseph's sons (Genesis 41:51-52), each get a portion in the land (Ezekiel 48:4-5), but the gate carries their father's name, Joseph.
